the performance of machine-learning-based vulnerability detection is influenced by four factors, i.e., datasets, classification models, vectorization methods and user-defined variable and name replacement.

the quality of vulnerability datasets and classification models, as well as vectorization methods, can directly affect the performance of vulnerability detectors, in contrast, function/variable name replacements can affect the features and indirectly affect the detection performance.

(1) deep learning models can achieve higher accuracy than traditional machine learning methods, and (2) datasets with user-defined variable name replacement can significantly affect the features of code and decrease the performance of machine-learning-based vulnerability detection.
